page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-32 is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by 64-bit Arm architecture. Built upon the Ampere AmpereOne processor family, this configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. Each virtual CPU corresponds to an entire physical core with a single thread per core, preventing resource contention commonly found in simultaneous multithreading environments. The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance profile features no bundled local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Persistent data persistence and file systems must be connected over network-attached block storage volumes. External network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The absence of local solid-state drives minimizes hypervisor-level storage overhead, focusing resources entirely on compute execution and in-memory operations.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides an efficient architecture for workloads requiring higher memory density relative to core count. Given the balance of dedicated Arm cores and 32.0 GB of capacity, the instance serves in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational and NoSQL databases, memory-intensive CI/CD build environments, and containerized microservices running on native 64-bit Arm platforms.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-32 is an Arm-based cloud virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive computing tasks. Driven by Ampere AmpereOne processors clocked at 3.0 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution, removing cross-thread contention. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a generous 1:8 core-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage and operates without GPU hardware acceleration, instead relying on networked block volumes for persistent data needs and including one complimentary public IPv4 address. Its dedicated core allocation and dense memory footprint make it a viable, cost-effective resource for Arm-native development, memory-resident databases, caching services, and web application runtimes.
